statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java 2D partial-denial-of-service issue. Both open PR #5075 and PR #5078 incorrectly treated this as already covered by merged PR #5071 (likely conflated with CVE-2026-47021, also a "2D" component JSSE-adjacent issue assessed there) -- it was not actually present in #5071 or on main, so this closes that gap. The scanned image reports Oracle OpenJDK 21.0.11+10-LTS; Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (docker/Dockerfile:2). A source review found no java.awt or 2D API usage anywhere in the shipped runtime path, matching the code_not_reachable finding already recorded for CVE-2026-47021 and CVE-2026-47010 (same "2D"/ "ImageIO" component family). Oracle's own advisory note for this CVE goes further than the boilerplate applet note used elsewhere: it explicitly states the issue "does not apply to Java deployments, typically in servers, that load and run only trusted code (e.g., code installed by an administrator)" -- which is exactly Liquibase Secure's deployment model (a headless CLI running only its own installed code, not a sandboxed client executing untrusted 2D content).

statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE Security (java.security) issue, fixed in OpenJDK 21.0.12. The JRE was read from the release file of each published Liquibase Secure image: 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.8, 5.0.2 and 5.0.3 ship 21.0.9, 5.1.0 and 5.1.1 ship 21.0.10, 5.2.0 and 5.2.1 ship 21.0.11, 5.2.2 ships 21.0.12+8 and 6.0.0 ships 21.0.12.1+1, so 5.2.2 and later already carry the fix. For the earlier images, exploitation needs an attacker to deliver crafted data to the java.security APIs, either through a network service that passes untrusted input to them or through a sandboxed Java Web Start or applet client that runs untrusted code. Liquibase Secure is neither. It runs as a command-line client that starts no listener, runs no untrusted code, and only connects outbound to the database and service endpoints its operator configures.

statements.impact_statement: JDK Security component (resource resolving) vulnerability, part of Oracle's August 2026 CPU. Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse- temurin:21-jre-noble (docker/Dockerfile:2) and never listens on a socket; it is only an outbound network client (HTTPS to license/hub endpoints, TLS JDBC to target databases). Triggering this requires a compromised or MITM'd peer that Liquibase already trusts and connects to -- not exploitable by an arbitrary remote attacker with no foothold on those endpoints. Fixed upstream in Temurin 21.0.12.1+1, but no eclipse- temurin Docker Hub image publishes that build yet as of 2026-09-22 (all noble/jre/jdk tags remain 21.0.12_8); revisit once Temurin ships an updated 21-jre-noble tag.

statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE/GraalVM Install-component vulnerability, fixed upstream in 21.0.12 (Oracle August 2026 CPU). The flaw is in Oracle's Java installer, a packaging component that ships only with Oracle's own distribution. Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (core/docker/Dockerfile:1) via docker-entrypoint.sh (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8); Temurin's JRE is unpacked from a release archive, not installed through Oracle's installer, so the vulnerable component is not present in the image at all. There is no Adoptium/Temurin tracking entry for this CVE. Unlike the other Oracle Java SE entries in this batch (sandbox/Web Start applicability mismatches, justified requires_environment), this is a component absence -- the installer isn't shipped at all -- hence code_not_present.
